paragraphs: In Solihull, children in care live with foster carers approved by Solihull Council or by independent fostering agencies such as those listed on this page. The council recruits for short-term fostering while courts decide a child's future, long-term fostering until 18 or independence, emergency care at short notice, and respite at weekends or in school holidays. It also has specialist carers for unaccompanied asylum-seeking young people, who are mostly in their mid to late teens, and says it often needs homes for brothers and sisters who come into care together.

Family Links is the council's short breaks service for disabled children up to 18. Carers offer stays of up to 24 hours or two nights, and commit to at least two nights a month plus extra in the school holidays. Relevant experience can come from volunteering, work or family life. Relatives and friends can also be approved as kinship foster carers.

Every Solihull carer has a supervising social worker based in the borough, with access to a nurse for children in care, education support, local training alongside social workers, and yearly celebration events. The council pays a fee for each child in placement plus an allowance towards the child's needs.

The council says becoming a carer takes around six months, from a home visit and pre-approval training through a two-stage assessment to the fostering panel. Speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and compare the training, support and pay each offers.
